title: Soapbox's Vision: Why Volumetric Video is Poised to Transform Music, One Headset at a Time
summary: Soapbox is pioneering volumetric video technology to create "life-size holograms" of artists, offering a glimpse into a more immersive musical future. Despite current industry skepticism towards VR/AR, the company firmly believes that next-generation AR glasses will be the catalyst that finally brings this transformative experience to the mainstream.
content:
Let's be frank: the music industry isn't exactly buzzing with excitement over virtual and augmented reality right now. After several high-profile attempts and a handful of lukewarm receptions, many have quietly filed VR and AR under "interesting but not quite there yet" when it comes to revolutionizing how we consume music.

Yet, tucked away from the mainstream spotlight, innovators like Soapbox are quietly building the foundations for what they believe will be a seismic shift. Their secret sauce? Volumetric video. Imagine filming an artist not just in 2D, but capturing them in full 3D space, allowing that footage to be transformed into stunning, “life-size holograms” capable of performing on any virtual stage, or even in your living room.

While the current applications might still feel a little niche – think interactive installations or bespoke VR experiences – Soapbox's vision extends far beyond. The real game-changer, they contend, isn't the content itself, but the hardware that brings it to life. “The glasses will change the game,” a bold statement that cuts through the current skepticism, pointing to a future where lightweight, powerful AR glasses become as ubiquitous as smartphones.

This isn't just about watching a concert; it's about shared experiences, about bringing artists closer to fans in ways never before possible, blurring the lines between the digital and physical. Picture an artist appearing as a hologram in your friend's living room, or a collaborative performance spanning continents, all made possible by advanced AR eyewear seamlessly integrated into our daily lives.

In an era where many have written off music's AR/VR potential, Soapbox's unwavering belief in volumetric video and the impending wave of consumer-friendly AR glasses offers a compelling counter-narrative. They aren't just creating content; they're laying the groundwork for a truly immersive future where our favorite artists might just be a holographic tap away.
keyTakeaways: Soapbox is leveraging volumetric video technology to create "life-size holograms" of musical artists.
Despite current industry disinterest in VR/AR for music, Soapbox believes future AR glasses will be the pivotal factor for mainstream adoption.
This technology aims to redefine live music and fan engagement by offering immersive, interactive experiences that blur the lines between physical and digital reality.
author: Stuart Dredge

title: Music's Next Dimension: Why Soapbox Thinks AR Glasses Will Unleash Holographic Artists
summary: Soapbox is pioneering the use of volumetric video to create "life-size holograms" of musical artists, aiming to revolutionize fan engagement. Despite current industry skepticism towards VR/AR, the company believes advanced AR glasses will be the game-changer, integrating these immersive performances seamlessly into daily life.
content:
The year 2026 has hardly been a banner year for virtual and augmented reality in the music industry. Despite persistent predictions and numerous early attempts to integrate these immersive technologies into artist experiences and fan engagement, widespread adoption remains elusive, leaving many industry watchers skeptical. The clunky headsets and often solitary nature of current VR have largely failed to ignite the mass market enthusiasm once envisioned.

Enter Soapbox, a company quietly but powerfully challenging this narrative. They're leveraging cutting-edge volumetric video technology to capture artists performing and interacting, then transforming that raw footage into incredibly lifelike, "life-size holograms." This isn't just a fancy video effect; it’s about creating a tangible presence of an artist in a virtual or augmented space, offering a profound sense of immersion that traditional video can't match.

Soapbox's vision hinges on a crucial future development: the widespread adoption of advanced AR glasses. As one Soapbox executive succinctly put it, "The glasses will change the game." Current VR headsets, while powerful, isolate users. True AR glasses, however, promise to seamlessly blend digital content with our physical world, allowing an artist's holographic performance to appear right in a fan’s living room, shared with friends, or integrated into live events.

This shift from isolating VR to pervasive AR could unlock unprecedented creative and commercial opportunities. Imagine experiencing a private, intimate concert with your favorite musician’s hologram, or attending a global virtual festival where artists from across the world perform "live" in your space. For artists, it means new avenues for fan interaction, merchandise, and even entirely new forms of digital art and storytelling, moving beyond the confines of traditional screens and venues. Soapbox is betting that when the hardware truly enables a natural, collective immersive experience, the music industry’s skepticism will finally give way to revolutionary engagement.
keyTakeaways: Soapbox uses volumetric video to create realistic, "life-size holograms" of artists for immersive experiences.
The company identifies advanced AR glasses, not current VR headsets, as the crucial technology for widespread adoption in the music industry.
This technology promises to unlock new forms of fan interaction, artistic expression, and revenue streams for musicians.
author: Stuart Dredge
